context: Sortable data table showing book chapter sentence rhythm, with per-row sparklines (sentence sequence) and mini violin plots (sentence-length distribution) — a data visualization combining multiple encodings.
first_impression: Clean, functional table with a restrained single-hue palette and real typographic hierarchy, but the violin plots are too small to extract distributional meaning and the overall feel is competent rather than designed.
what_works: Deliberate color restraint — one muted blue (#4a7cb5) for both sparklines and violins with a single red accent only for the longest-sentence marker — shows genuine palette intention. Typographic hierarchy is real: 18px bold title, 13px gray subtitle, 11px uppercase letter-spaced column headers, 13px body text.
what_doesnt: Violin plots at 100×32px are too small to compare distributions across rows — the shapes are barely distinguishable and subtle differences (bimodality, skew) are lost at that height. The sparklines lack any axis reference line or baseline, so the shared y-scale (which does exist in code) is invisible to the reader, leaving sentence-length magnitude unreadable without hovering.
